items.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Alfred was going to call the date off. I told Alfred to wait and let me talk to the band.

ctx.x: Your own music really – not really started changing, but there was these three albums that – I think this is the stuff that – this is where I came into really hearing you. Everything else from this point was going backward or going forward. You care to comment on Let Freedom Ring and One Step Beyond and Destination . . . Out!?

Let Freedom Ring was a quintet, originally a quintet album. Donald got sick on the date, couldn’t play. So he left. Alfred was going to call the date off. I told Alfred to wait and let me talk to the band. I said, “That don’t make sense, to call it off.” So I went to talk to the guys. I say, “We can do this thing without the trumpet,” and we did it. That was it. I went to Alfred. I said, “Man, we don’t need the trumpet. We can do it without the trumpet.”

One thing that hit me on that album is it’s the first time I heard you go way above the natural range of the alto, almost into a place where you’re whistling, a whistling thing. Was – what was . . . ?
